headline: Sales growth broadens into margin and profit gains
summary_short: Ollie's Q1 fiscal 2026 net sales rose 14.2% y/y to $658.9M on new-store growth and a 1.7% comp-sales gain, while operating income grew 23.8% to $69.6M and diluted EPS rose to $0.92 from $0.77.
summary_long: Net sales grew on new-unit growth (27 stores opened, ending at 672 stores in 35 states) plus a 1.7% comparable-store-sales increase driven by higher basket size. Gross margin expanded 80bp to 41.9% on lower supply chain costs and slightly better merchandise margin. SG&A held flat at 28.6% of sales despite absolute growth from new-store costs; pre-opening expense fell on lower dark-rent from fewer bankruptcy-acquired stores. Net income rose 18.6% to $56.4M despite a higher effective tax rate (24.3% vs 22.0%) tied to expiring tax credits. The company repurchased $53.4M of stock and spent $25.5M on capex, ending the quarter with $249.6M of cash and short-term investments. This 10-Q contains no forward guidance.

drivers.explanation: Sales, margins, and profit all improved on new-store growth and a modest comp-sales gain, with operating leverage lifting EBITDA and net income faster than revenue.
Net sales growth was the result of new store unit growth and a 1.7% comparable-store-sales increase, which was itself driven by an increase in basket size.
Gross margin rose 80 basis points to 41.9%, driven by lower supply chain costs and a modest increase in merchandise margin.
SG&A grew 14.5% on higher new-store-related selling costs but held flat as a share of sales; pre-opening expense fell on lower dark rent from fewer bankruptcy-acquired stores.
EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA grew faster than revenue, tracking the gross-margin expansion and operating-income improvement described above.
Net income growth was tempered by a higher effective tax rate (24.3% vs 22.0%), driven by the impact of discrete items including the expiration of the Work Opportunity Tax Credit.
